documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive shortness of breath and leg swelling x 5 days.
HPI:
58 yo F with known HFrEF (EF 30% on echo 4 months ago), HTN, DM2, CKD stage 3 presents to ED with worsening dyspnea.
Symptoms began roughly 1 week ago with exertional dyspnea climbing stairs, progressed to dyspnea at rest by this morning.
Orthopnea requiring 3 pillows; 2 episodes of PND overnight.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Denies chest pain, fever, cough productive of sputum, hemoptysis. Reports palpitations starting yesterday evening.
Reports dietary indiscretion at a family gathering 1 week ago - canned soup, cured ham.
No recent travel, no leg pain, no syncope.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
New atrial fibrillation with RVR, heart rate 138; started diltiazem drip; on continuous telemetry.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
1. HFrEF, EF 30%, nonischemic per cath 2 yrs ago
2. Hypertension
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus, last A1c 7.8%
4. CKD stage 3, baseline creatinine 1.3
5. Obesity
6. Obstructive sleep apnea - CPAP prescribed, pt reports intermittent use
HOME MEDICATIONS:
furosemide 80 mg PO BID (recently doubled)
carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
sacubitril-valsartan 49-51 mg PO BID
spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
metformin 1000 mg PO BID
SOCIAL:
Lives with daughter. Former smoker, quit 8 yrs ago, approx 20 pack-yrs. No alcohol. No illicits.
FAMILY HISTORY: Mother with CHF, father with MI in his 60s.
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
Positive for dyspnea, orthopnea, leg edema, palpitations, fatigue, abdominal fullness, decreased appetite.
Negative for fever, chills, chest pain, melena, dysuria, focal weakness.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Vitals: BP 148/92, HR 138 irregular, T 36.8, SpO2 91% on 4L NC.
Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
Gen: ill-appearing, sitting upright, diaphoretic.
HEENT: JVD to angle of jaw at 45 degrees. Mucous membranes moist.
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, tachycardic, no murmur appreciated over tachycardia, S3 questionable.
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally, dullness to percussion at both bases, no wheeze.
Abd: soft, mildly distended, tender RUQ, hepatomegaly 3 cm below costal margin.
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, cool distally, cap refill 3 sec.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit.
LABS:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago).
Na 133, K 4.1, Cl 96, HCO3 24, BUN 42, glucose 168.
WBC 8.2, Hgb 11.4, Plt 208.
Troponin 0.04 then 0.05 - flat, not consistent with ACS.
TSH pending. Mg 1.8. LFTs: AST 44, ALT 38, T bili 1.4, albumin 3.3.
IMAGING/ECG:
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
ECG: atrial fibrillation at 138, no acute ST changes, LVH by voltage.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
58 yo F with acute decompensated HFrEF, volume overloaded, with new onset AF with RVR and acute kidney injury on CKD.
1. Acute decompensated HF - continue IV furosemide 80 mg q12h, strict I/O, daily weights, fluid restrict 1.5 L, Na <2 g.
2. New AF with RVR - diltiazem drip, telemetry, rate goal <110. Hold carvedilol while on drip. Anticoagulation to be discussed w cardiology.
3. Hypoxic respiratory failure - 4L NC, wean as able, monitor for BiPAP need.
4. AKI on CKD - hold sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone, trend BMP q12h, avoid nephrotoxins.
5. DM2 - hold metformin and empagliflozin, SSI q6h.
6. Consulted cardiology this evening, will see in AM.
Admit to stepdown unit for telemetry and close monitoring.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 - Cardiology/Hospitalist
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports breathing somewhat improved overnight but still dyspneic with minimal exertion. Slept upright in chair part of night. Palpitations less noticeable.
Reports urinating but not as much as expected. No chest pain.
OVERNIGHT EVENTS:
HR down to 96-108 on diltiazem drip at 10 mg/hr. No sustained RVR episodes.
Urine output 470 mL over prior 24 hours despite two 80 mg IV doses.
OBJECTIVE:
Vitals: BP 132/80, HR 102 irregular, T 36.6, RR 24.
Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2, SpO2 92%.
Weight 96.8 kg, up 0.3 kg from admission weight.
Gen: less diaphoretic, speaking in short sentences.
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, rate controlled.
Lungs: crackles persist to mid fields, decreased breath sounds at bases.
Ext: 3+ pitting edema unchanged to mid thigh.
LABS:
Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2. BUN 51, K 4.4, Na 131, HCO3 23.
Mg 2.0 after repletion. Troponin not repeated - flat pattern.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Acute decompensated HFrEF, diuretic resistant. Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Add metolazone 5 mg PO x1 this morning. Goal net negative 1.5-2 L/24h. Recheck BMP at 18:00.
2. Worsening creatinine felt to be cardiorenal physiology/venous congestion rather than prerenal - continue decongestion.
3. AF - continue diltiazem drip, transition to oral dilt when stable. Started apixaban 5 mg BID after discussion w cardiology, CHA2DS2-VASc 4.
4. Hypoxia - continue 4L NC, wean as UOP improves. Nocturnal CPAP resumed.
5. Continue holding sacubitril-valsartan, spironolactone, metformin, empagliflozin.
6. Foley placed for accurate output measurement. DVT ppx covered by apixaban.
Discussed plan with pt and daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5 - Hospitalist
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports markedly improved breathing. Walked hallway approx 150 feet with RN yesterday without stopping. Sleeping flat with 1 pillow.
Appetite returning. No palpitations, no chest pain, no lightheadedness.
OBJECTIVE:
Vitals: BP 118/72, HR 78 regular rate, T 36.7, RR 18, SpO2 95% on RA.
Off supplemental O2 since HD4 09:00; ambulatory SpO2 93% on RA.
Weight 90.1 kg, down 6.7 kg from admission. Net negative 6.4 L cumulative.
Urine output 2,150 mL in past 24h.
Cardiac: rate controlled, telemetry shows sinus with rare PACs since HD4 14:00.
Lungs: scattered fine crackles at bases only, no accessory muscle use.
Ext: 1+ edema to ankles bilaterally.
JVD no longer appreciable at 45 degrees.
LABS:
Creatinine 1.6, BUN 34, K 3.8, Na 136, HCO3 26. Mg 2.1.
Repeat BNP 620 pg/mL.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Decompensated HFrEF - substantially decongested. Furosemide infusion stopped HD4 20:00, now on furosemide 80 mg IV BID, plan transition to PO today.
2. Renal function improving toward baseline with decongestion. Restarted sacubitril-valsartan 24-26 mg BID at reduced dose HD4; monitor BMP daily.
3. Atrial fibrillation - converted to sinus spontaneously HD4. Diltiazem drip off HD3, now diltiazem ER 180 mg daily. Carvedilol 6.25 mg BID resumed.
Continue apixaban 5 mg BID.
4. Hold spironolactone until Cr closer to baseline.
5. DM2 - restarted metformin HD4, SSI continued, glucoses 130-170.
6. Foley removed HD4, voiding without difficulty.
7. PT eval today. Nutrition consult done for low Na diet teaching.
Anticipate discharge tomorrow if weight and renal function stable on oral regimen.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure with New AF
lines: ADMITTING DIAGNOSIS: Acute decompensated heart failure
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute decompensated HFrEF, EF 30%, with hypoxic respiratory failure
2. New onset atrial fibrillation with RVR, now sinus rhythm
3. Acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3, resolving
4. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
5. Hypertension; OSA
LENGTH OF STAY: HD1 to HD6, discharged HD6.
HOSPITAL COURSE:

58 yo F with HFrEF presented with progressive dyspnea and edema. Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
At presentation: Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL). Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago), 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2.
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
New atrial fibrillation with RVR, heart rate 138; started diltiazem drip; on continuous telemetry. Converted to sinus rhythm HD4; transitioned to oral diltiazem ER.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Metolazone 5 mg x1 added HD2 with brisk response. Infusion stopped HD4, transitioned to oral diuretic HD5.
Total net negative 7.2 L over stay. Discharge weight 89.4 kg, down 7.4 kg from admission.
Creatinine improved to 1.4 mg/dL on day of discharge. Repeat BNP 620 pg/mL on HD5.
Weaned off supplemental oxygen HD4; ambulatory SpO2 94% on RA at discharge.
Apixaban started HD2 for AF, CHA2DS2-VASc 4. No bleeding complications.
DISCHARGE EXAM: BP 114/70, HR 74, RR 16, SpO2 94% RA. Lungs clear except trace basilar crackles. 1+ ankle edema. No JVD.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
furosemide 80 mg PO BID
carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
sacubitril-valsartan 24-26 mg PO BID
diltiazem ER 180 mg PO daily
apixaban 5 mg PO BID
atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily, metformin 1000 mg PO BID, empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
Spironolactone held at discharge, to be reassessed in clinic.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Daily weights same time each morning; call if weight up 1.5 kg in 2 days or 2.5 kg in a week.
Sodium under 2 g/day, fluid limit 1.5 L/day. Nightly CPAP use.
Call or return for worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations, bleeding, or chest pain.
FOLLOW UP: Cardiology in 5 days with BMP; primary care in 2 weeks. Home nursing arranged for weight and vitals checks.
Discharge instructions reviewed with pt and daughter; both verbalized understanding.
